title: Learning from Emergence: A Study on Proactively Inhibiting the Monosemantic Neurons of Artificial Neural Networks

problem.claim: Monosemantic neurons may be a key factor affecting performance as model scale increases, but their role and mitigation require investigation.

gap.claim: There is no unified quantitative metric for evaluating monosemanticity, and simply banning monosemantic neurons does not promote polysemanticity.

contributions.claim: A metric is proposed to measure neuron monosemanticity with efficient online computation.
A theoretically supported training method is introduced to suppress monosemantic neurons and promote polysemantic neurons.
The study examines the relationship between monosemanticity and performance across model scales, neural networks, benchmark datasets, and language, image, and physics simulation tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present a new monosemanticity metric and a proactive inhibition method for promoting polysemanticity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validating their conjecture across different model scales, neural networks, benchmark datasets, and language, image, and physics simulation tasks.
The authors report that further experiments support their analysis and theory concerning inhibition of monosemanticity.

narrative_sequence.summary: The authors hypothesize that reducing monosemantic neurons helps explain performance changes with increasing model scale.
They identify the lack of a unified metric and the insufficiency of simply banning monosemantic neurons.
They propose an efficient monosemanticity metric and a theoretically supported training method to inhibit monosemantic neurons.
They report evaluations across model scales, neural networks, datasets, and multiple application areas, followed by experiments addressing their analysis and theory.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links neuron-level monosemanticity to performance changes across model scales.

interpretation.claim: Representation characteristics may provide a mechanism for studying how scaling affects model performance.

application.claim: When analyzing scaling behavior, measure and monitor representation properties alongside aggregate performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that monosemanticity is the sole or universally causal factor.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the metric definition or theoretical guarantees.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, model configurations, or statistical details.
The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets or neural network architectures.
